claim: LLM false-belief scores rise sharply with model scale on standard tasks (0% for GPT-1/2 up to 75% for GPT-4 on 40 all-or-nothing tasks; 97% on ToM-k items), but this is not robust mind-tracking.
agent_test: Run our agent on paired false-belief plus true-belief controls at equal tokens; report only all-correct tasks.

claim: Trivial alterations (transparent bag, informed protagonist, sighted character) break models that pass the base task, so standard ToM scores overstate competence; some of the effect is shortcut use.
agent_test: Build altered variants of each social probe; count the agent as passing only if base and altered variants both pass.

claim: Kosinski's own controls and variant checks show the base items are partly solved by word-order cues in older models, while GPT-4 handles most control variants; the interpretation of 75% is contested (ToM vs. shortcut).
agent_test: Same variant battery; compare accuracy drop base to altered for scaffold versus plain.

claim: Explicit mental-state questions are answered well (over 95%) while applying that knowledge to predict or judge behaviour lags by 30+ points and judgment falls below chance for frontier non-reasoning models; reasoning models (o1-preview 84.1% on prediction) close most of the gap.
agent_test: Ask the agent both 'what does X believe' and 'what will X do / was X reasonable'; measure the knowing-doing gap with and without scaffold.

claim: Prompts that tell the model to track the relevant mental state help: a reminder lifts behaviour prediction above 80%, and perspective-taking (SimToM) gives large gains on ToMI/BigToM for GPT-3.5 (+47 and +29.5 points over 0-shot CoT / 0-shot) but small gains on GPT-4 and a loss in a single-prompt variant.
agent_test: Add an explicit 'filter to what this agent knows' step before answering any question about another party; test at equal tokens against one-prompt CoT.
gap_search_note: Thought-tracing (Kim 2025) is a second independent explicit-mental-state routine that beats CoT and several reasoning models at fewer tokens.

claim: Generic chain of thought does not reliably help on social reasoning: it helped some models on FANToM and BigToM, gave +3.6 / -0.09 on Hi-ToM, lowered accuracy on deception stories, and left the gap to humans (87.5 vs 26.6) large.
agent_test: Compare plain CoT with the scaffold on the social items; do not count on CoT alone.
gap_search_note: Vanilla CoT lowers true-belief scores in closed models (GPT-4o 80.5 to 58.0); reasoning models near 100 on false belief, under 50 on true belief.

claim: Higher-order (nested) belief and interactive conversation tracking are far weaker than first-order: all Hi-ToM models under 60% and joint accuracy at third order and above about 0.05-0.35; FANToM best zero-shot GPT-4 14.8-26.6 vs human 87.5.
agent_test: Test nested-belief depth (order 1-4) with the agent; log where accuracy collapses.

claim: Humans and GPT-4 differ by test type: GPT-4 matches or beats humans on irony and strange stories but is below humans on faux pas (r=0.55), partly from caution about committing, not inability; LLaMA2-70B's faux-pas edge looks like a bias.
agent_test: Re-run the faux-pas likelihood framing on our agent; check for refusal-to-commit bias.
gap_search_note: Strachan full text opened: 1,907 humans in follow-ups; faux pas 2 of 349 GPT answers said speaker knew; likelihood wording GPT-4 100%.

claim: Intrinsic self-correction without an external signal does not improve reasoning and often lowers it (GPT-3.5 CSQA 75.8 to 38.1 then 41.8; GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 to 89.0); it helps only with an oracle label.
agent_test: Compare a revise-own-answer step against an external check at equal tokens; consistent with our G1 doubt result (92% to 75%).
gap_search_note: Independent support: Tyen 2024 (finding the mistake is the bottleneck; oracle location +23.5 to +43.9 on incorrect traces, but -6.7 to -11.4 on correct ones) and Kamoi 2024 survey (no prompt-only success); SCoRe shows it is trainable. No reasoning-model replication with external control found.

claim: Metacognitive prompting (a five-step self-evaluation prompt) gives modest gains over CoT on NLU (BoolQ 89.0 vs 86.3; EUR-LEX up to +26.9) but 31.7% of its errors are overcorrection and 68.3% overthinking.
agent_test: Test whether a bounded self-check step beats CoT at equal tokens and measure overcorrection rate.

claim: Metacognitive therapy has very large effects against waitlist (g=2.06, k=9) and moderate effects against CBT that shrink at follow-up (g=0.69 to 0.37; trim-and-fill 0.53), with possible allegiance bias (Wells-group 1.98 vs independent 1.49) and weak allocation-concealment reporting.
agent_test: None for the agent; clinical evidence only. Do not import MCT as an agent mechanism.
gap_search_note: 2025-2026 trials: Pakistani OCD RCT (independent, vs TAU, g -1.12 to -1.54), Norwegian sick-leave RCT (waitlist, Wells co-author); against active ERP (Exner, N=74) non-inferior at post, not confirmed at 6 months; independent Swedish tMCT vs CBT trial still a protocol.

claim: MCT shows benefit across conditions in separate trials (GAD recovery 67% vs 43% in one meta-analysis, depression RCT d=2.51, return-to-work OR 2.39, OCD Y-BOCS -6.92 at 6 months, PTSD g=2.88), but the OCD trial did not support the belief-change mediator and the PTSD pool was heterogeneous.
agent_test: None directly; a reminder that mechanism claims (changing metacognitive beliefs) are weaker than outcome claims.
gap_search_note: Stand-alone detached mindfulness meta-analysis: g -1.80, k=3 clinical trials.

claim: Metacognitive training for psychosis has small effects (positive symptoms g=0.50, hallucinations 0.26, cognitive biases 0.16) and benefit depends on baseline cognitive insight (13 studies, 614 participants).
agent_test: None for the agent.

claim: Two-person groups gain over the better member only when partners are of similar sensitivity and communicate confidence in words; with unequal skill the pair does worse than the better member, and adding a non-verbal confidence tool reduced performance.
agent_test: Test an ensemble of two agent runs with a weak and a strong member: does confidence-weighted merge beat the strong member alone at equal total tokens?

claim: Homogeneous multi-agent LLM debate is a martingale with no expected gain and can fall below majority vote (Qwen-7B GSM8K 0.847 vs 0.908); diversity plus confidence restores gains (GSM8K 0.932).
agent_test: Compare debate between identical copies, diverse copies, and majority vote at equal tokens.

claim: Third-person confidence reading matches self-evaluation in humans (hetero-metacognition equals self-metacognition) in one auditory study.
agent_test: Check whether the agent's reading of another run's confidence beats its own self-rating.

claim: LLM token-level self-knowledge is reasonably calibrated: filtering answers with P(True) above 0.5 improves accuracy, with AUROC in the 0.6-0.85 range.
agent_test: Use own-probability filtering as a cheap abstain gate; test at equal tokens.

claim: LLM cognitive-reframing and CBT tools show measured gains in text overlap and expert-rated empathy, but chatbot dialogs show shallow reframing ('maybe' treated as agreement); no study applies Wells' metacognitive therapy to LLMs.
agent_test: None; sources are about therapy chatbots, not the agent's own thinking.

claim: Demetriou-style development (g shifting from executive to inferential to self-awareness processes with age) is a human developmental claim with no LLM test found.
agent_test: None.

claim: Reasoning models do not solve social reasoning: o1, o3-mini and R1 score near 100 on false-belief items but under 50 (sometimes under 30) on matching true-belief items, and a structured thought-tracing wrapper on GPT-4o beats most of them at far fewer tokens (ToMi 76.0 vs o1-medium 70.8, o3-mini-medium 64.0, R1 68.3).
agent_test: Always pair each false-belief probe with a true-belief twin; compare scaffold tracing vs a reasoning-effort increase at equal tokens.

claim: In the Strachan battery GPT-4's faux pas failure is over-caution, not failed inference: the yes/no knowledge question gets 'not enough information' (only 2 of 349 answers said the speaker knew), but 'which is more likely' gets 100% unprompted.
agent_test: Phrase social probes as most-likely-state questions and compare with yes/no phrasing.

claim: In MCT for OCD, an independent 2026 RCT (N=76) found large symptom benefit vs treatment as usual but no support for the claimed mechanism: metacognitive belief change did not temporally mediate symptom change (indirect beta=-0.01). Against ERP, MCT was non-inferior at post but not confirmed at 6 months (Exner, second-hand).
agent_test: None for the agent; reason not to port MCT mechanisms.

claim: Gaps 3, 5, 8 and 9 have no direct evidence: no LLM test of Bahrami-style confidence-weighted merging, no LLM test of detached mindfulness or worry postponement, no link between Demetriou's developmental order and LLM capability order, and no Hi-ToM order 3+ result for reasoning models were found (search-limited: APIs rate-limited, WebSearch spent).
agent_test: Run our own two-run merge test and a detach-from-draft prompt test; both are untested ideas, not findings.
